question: At each site, how do the recorded dates of the management events sit against the change of daily GPP, Reco and NEE, and against the crop calendar of field crop production?

rules: Sites: Anttila, Sarkisuo, Haltiala, Qvidja, Viikki and Maktau (order of db/sites.parquet).
1. Local day = ts_start (UTC) + utc_offset_min. Daily air temperature and soil water content =
mean of the 30-min values of db/observations.parquet; daily precipitation = sum (null when
all half hours of the day are null). Daily GPP, Reco and gap-filled NEE (g C m-2 d-1), the
measured fraction of NEE and the daily mean air temperature for the season come from
data/calculated/daily.parquet. Days with a measured fraction below 0.10 are drawn lighter;
they are not removed. The timeline of a site is the period from the first to the last day
with a gap-filled NEE value.
2. Episodes: the events of one site form one episode when an event starts not more than 7 days
after the last day (date_end, else date) of the current episode. The event "EC system
installed" is not a field operation and is not in an episode. Start = first date, end = last
date_end (or date). Episode kind = the first type of this list that is in the episode:
harvest, cut, grazing, tillage, sowing, fertilisation, spraying, other. The anchor is the
first date of an event of the episode kind.
3. Before window = days -7 to -1 before the start; after window = days +1 to +7 after the end.
Change = mean after - mean before of daily GPP, Reco and NEE (g C m-2 d-1); GPP also in
percent of the GPP before (only when the GPP before is 1 g C m-2 d-1 or more). Each side needs
5 days with a value. An episode with a day of another episode in its windows is flagged
"overlap" and is not in the summaries.
4. Change point (port of detectDrop, scripts/lib/deep-dive/change-point.ts): for each candidate
day t, step(t) = sign * (mean of days t-5..t-1 - mean of days t..t+4), each side with 4 or
more values. The detected day is the t with the largest step (the first on a tie). The step
is clear when the higher side (the side before for a drop, the side after for a rise) has a
mean of 1 g C m-2 d-1 or more and the step is 25 % or more of it. Tests: harvest, cut,
grazing and tillage episodes: largest GPP drop for t from start - 10 to end + 5. Episodes
with a sowing: largest GPP rise for t from the sowing date to the sowing date + 40 days.
Episodes with a tillage: also the largest Reco rise from start - 10 to end + 5.
Fertilisation, spraying and other: no change point. Offset = detected day - anchor (days;
negative = the flux changed before the recorded date). An episode is not in the offset
summaries when another episode with a change-point test (harvest, cut, grazing, tillage,
sowing) has a day in the days that the search reads (start - 15 to end + 9).
Check on measured NEE: daily mean of the measured NEE (nee_qc 0 or null, nee not null) of
the half hours that start from 10:00 to 15:30 local time, 8 or more half hours per day;
largest drop of -NEE in the same span (3 or more values per side, higher side 1 umol m-2
s-1 or more). The two change points agree when they differ by 1 day or less.
5. Alternative dates (ALTERNATIVE_DATES, typed from the sources): the same change-point search,
on the candidate days within -10 .. +5 days of the used date and of the other date
(the other event gets the same duration as the used one). Candidates whose 10 side days
touch another episode are skipped. The result gives the offset to each date and the date
that is nearer to the detected day. It also gives the files of the source column of
db/events.parquet that give the date in the database (sourceUsed: the files of the
event without the file of the other date; all files when both dates come from one file).
5b. Wide second dates (second_dates.py, |days apart| > 12): for the database date and the
other date, the mean of GPP, Reco, NEE, measured day-time -NEE, air temperature and soil
water over the 7 days before the first day and the 7 days after the end day, the change
and the percent change, the precipitation sums, and the lowest and highest daily GPP of
the span (10 days before the earlier date to 10 days after the later end day).
6. Summaries per site and kind and per kind: n, mean, SD, median, range of the offset of the
clear change points, counts before (< 0), on (0) and after (> 0) the anchor, and the share of
clear tests. Bootstrap 95 % CI of the mean (10 000 resamples, percentile method, numpy
PCG64, fixed seeds) when n >= 3, else only the range. The same for the 7-day changes.
7. Thermal growing season (Finnish sites; the +5 degC rule of Peltokasvien tuotanto, ch.
2.1.1): start = first day from 1 March on with a daily mean above 5 degC on that day and the
next 9 days (all 10 days with a value); end = first day from 1 August on with a daily mean
below 5 degC on 10 such days. No start when the data of the year begin after 1 March.
Maktau: months with a precipitation sum above 50 mm (our rule) are drawn as bands.
8. Each step that removes rows or changes values logs a count (results.json dataVersion.steps).
9. Open findings of docs/anomaly-data-report.md that touch this dive are printed (OPEN_FINDINGS).
openFindings: ANT-01, SAR-01, VII-01 (open, waits for the providers): the raw stamps of Anttila, Sarkisuo and Viikki are UTC, but the build reads them as UTC+2. A local day of these sites thus starts at 02:00 true local time, and the measured NEE window 10:00 to 15:30 is 12:00 to 17:30 true local time. A daily change point can move by not more than 1 day.
VII-05 (open): Viikki 2024 nee_f is not equal to nee in 1 540 periods. The gap filling around the 2024 events can thus differ from the measured values.
QVI-08 (open): the Qvidja rain gauge has a gap from 2021-12-29 to 2022-05-24; the precipitation strip is empty there.
QVI-09 (known): all Qvidja meteorology is lost from 2023-02-11 to 2023-03-01 (no event in this period).
MKT-01, MKT-02, MKT-03 (Maktau): night rows missing 2023-07 to 2024-01, vpd in fill rows, and repeated FC values 2024-04 to 2024-07. They are outside the Maktau event years (2019, 2020).

literature.text: The thermal growing season starts in spring when the daily mean temperature stays above +5 °C and ends in autumn when it falls below +5 °C.
literature.textFi: Terminen kasvukausi alkaa keväällä, kun vuorokauden keskilämpötila on ylittänyt pysyvästi +5 °C.

literature.text: The thermal growing season is 180 days in southern Finland and 110 days in the far north; in the south it starts on average at the end of April and ends in mid-October.
literature.textFi: Termisen kasvukauden pituus vaihtelee siten eteläisen Suomen 180 päivästä pohjoisimman Suomen 110 päivään.

literature.text: Growing time of a barley variety: 96 days in zone I (thermal season 170 to 180 days) and 83 to 87 days in zone IV.
literature.textFi: Ohralajikkeen kasvuaika (vrk): I 96, IV 83–87; termisen kasvukauden pituus I 170–180.

literature.text: Perennial crops use the thermal season better; grasses and winter cereals start to grow in spring when the temperature rises just above zero.
literature.textFi: nurmikasvit ja syysviljat aloittavat kasvun keväällä lämpötilan kohotessa juuri nollan yläpuolelle

literature.text: A dry spell after the first harvest slows or even prevents the regrowth of a forage ley, and the second yield stays small.
literature.textFi: ensimmäisen sadonkorjuun jälkeen ajoittunut kuivuusjakso hidastaa ja jopa estää jälkikasvun

literature.text: Cereals have a determinate growth habit and their yield ripens almost at the same time; pulses and oil crops have an indeterminate habit.
literature.textFi: Viljoilla, joilla on päätteellinen kasvutapa, sato tuleentuu lähes samanaikaisesti.

literature.text: Spring cereals (spring wheat, spring rye, barley and oats) are sown in April and May; they grow for one season and are harvested in late summer.
literature.textFi: kevätkylvöiset ... kylvetään keväällä huhti-toukokuussa ... niiden sato korjataan syyskesällä

literature.text: The earliest cereal varieties start to ripen at the end of July and late varieties can ripen only in September; at ripening the leaves die and dry.
literature.textFi: Heinäkuun lopulla aikaisimmat lajikkeet alkavat tuleentua. Tuleentumisen yhteydessä lehdet kuolevat ja kuivuvat.

literature.text: Spring cereals usually get their fertiliser in one application at sowing, as placement fertilisation.
literature.textFi: Kevätviljojen tarvitsema lannoitus annetaan yleensä yhtenä eränä kylvön yhteydessä sijoituslannoituksena.

literature.text: Growing time of fava bean: 111 days.
literature.textFi: Härkäpapu: kasvuaika 111 vrk

literature.text: In Finland, flowering of pea and fava bean starts in late June and continues to the end of July; the seed weight starts to increase about three weeks after flowering.
literature.textFi: Suomessa kukinta alkaa kesäkuun loppupuolella ja jatkuu aina heinäkuun loppuun.

literature.text: Forage leys that overwinter well are harvested for three to four years after the establishment year.
literature.textFi: Satoa hyvin talvehtineista rehunurmista korjataan perustamisvuoden jälkeen kolmen neljän vuoden ajan.

literature.text: Timothy regrows slowly, because its regrowth starts from the buds at the base of the shoots; fescues regrow fast.
literature.textFi: Timotei on jälkikasvultaan hidas, sillä sen jälkikasvu lähtee liikkeelle versojen tyvellä olevista silmuista.

literature.text: A cut removes the whole stand and with it the whole photosynthesising leaf area; regrowth uses the stored sugars and nitrogen at the base of the shoots.
literature.textFi: Koko kasvusto korjataan ja samalla menetetään koko yhteyttävä lehtipintaala.

literature.text: Forage grass is not harvested ripe like cereals; the harvest date follows the yield quantity and quality targets.
literature.textFi: Nurmirehua ei korjata viljojen tapaan tuleentuneena, vaan korjuuajankohta päätetään sadon määrällisten ja laadullisten tavoitteiden perusteella.

literature.text: Two or three forage yields are harvested from silage leys per season; the first is usually the largest; the regrowth stand is short and leafy and develops more slowly.
literature.textFi: Säilörehunurmista korjataan kasvukauden aikana kaksi tai kolme rehusatoa.

literature.text: Leys are established (sown) and renewed usually every 3 to 5 years.
literature.textFi: Nurmien viljelytoimiin kuuluu perustaminen eli kylvö ja uudistaminen yleensä 3–5 vuoden välein.

literature.text: Leys can be established in spring under a cover crop or in summer or autumn without a cover crop.
literature.textFi: Nurmet voidaan perustaa joko keväällä suojaviljaan tai kesällä tai syksyllä ilman suojaviljaa.

literature.text: Recommended nitrogen for a silage ley harvested three times on coarse mineral soils: 230 kg N/ha (pasture 190 kg N/ha).
literature.textFi: typpeä suositellaan karkeilla kivennäismailla kolme kertaa korjattavalle säilörehunurmelle 230 kg/ha

literature.text: In Finland, maize is best sown in the first or second week of May; it germinates only above 10 °C, emergence takes 2 to 4 weeks, and it usually flowers in July.
literature.textFi: Mikäli mahdollista, maissi kannattaa kylvää toukokuun ensimmäisen ja toisen viikon aikana.

literature.text: Annual carbon flows of a barley stand (about 4800 kg/ha yield): net photosynthesis 540, yield 300, litter and residues 150 g C m-2 yr-1; decomposer respiration about 230 g C m-2 yr-1. The annual carbon balance of crop production is about zero.
literature.textFi: Kasvituotannon hiilitase on vuosikierrossa likimäärin nolla

observations.rule: local day = ts_start + utc_offset_min; ta and swc = mean of the 30-min values; precip = sum (null when all are null); measured NEE = nee not null and nee_qc 0 or null, half hours that start from 10:00 to 15:30 local time, 8 or more per day

daily.rule: timeline = first to last day with nee_f_gc; days with frac_measured < 0.10 are drawn lighter

episodes.rule: overlap = a day of another episode in the 7-day windows (not in the summaries); spanOverlap = another episode with a change-point test in the days that the search reads (not in the offset summaries); searched = the test has at least one candidate day
